cards.title: Principles Over Techniques
cards.description: Understanding the 'why' behind every movement. A technique is situational. A principle applies everywhere; across weapons, ranges, and scenarios. Master the principle and the techniques follow. 'From one thing, know ten thousand things'.

cards.title: Make it Work
cards.description: You haven't really learned a skill if you can't make it work. A technique should be made operational by continuous drilling, pressure-testing, then refining based on what worked and what didn't. Learn, test, refine, repeat. 'All doubts must fall before a student can become a master'.

cards.title: Own It
cards.description: First, learn by doing what is shown, then by adapting it for yourself, and then you make it your own. Imitating your teacher can only take you so far. Absorb, internalize, until the art becomes your own expression. The ultimate goal is finding your own Lapunti.

cards.title: Traditional Knowledge, Modern Methods
cards.description: Respect and honor the art's roots and lineage, while structuring training for progressive learning, measurable growth, and easier absorption. The teacher is also a student, and I'm always on the lookout for effective ways of transmitting old wisdom using modern methodology.
